source_text:
Ἡμεῖς οὖν ἀραδιούργητον ἄγομεν τὴν ἡμέραν· μήτε προστιθέντες, μήτε ἀφαιρούμενοι. καὶ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν μεγάλα στοιχεῖα κεκοίμηται· ἅ τινα ἀναστήσεται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐν ᾗ ἔρχεται μετὰ δόξης ἐξ οὐρανῶν, καὶ ἀναστήσει πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους· Φίλιππον τὸν τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων, ὃς κεκοίμηται ἐν Ἱεραπόλει, καὶ δύο θυ γατέρες αὐτοῦ γεγηρακυῖαι παρθένοι· καὶ ἡ ἑτέρα αὐ τοῦ θυγάτηρ ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύ ματι πολιτευσαμένη, ὴ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἀναπαύεται· ἔτι δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ Κυρίου ἀναπεσών· ὃς ἐγενήθη ἱερεὺς τὸ πέταλον πεφορεκὼς, καὶ μάρτυς καὶ διδάσκαλος· οὗτος ἐν Ἐφέσῳ κεκοίμηται. ἔτι δὲ καὶ Πολύκαρπος ἐν Σμύρνῃ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος καὶ μάρ τυς· καὶ Θρασέας καὶ ἐπίσκοπος καὶ μάρτυς ἀπὸ Εὐμενείας, ὃς ἐν Σμύρνῃ κεκοίμηται. τί δὲ δεῖ λέγειν Σάγαριν ἐπίσκοπον καὶ μάρτυρα, ὃς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ κεκοίμηται; ἔτι δὲ καὶ Παπείριον τὸν μακάριον, καὶ Μελίτωνα τὸν εὐνοῦχον, τὸν ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύματι πάντα πολιτευσάμενον· ὃς κεῖται ἐν Σάρδεσι περιμένων τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐπισκοπὴν, ἐν ᾗ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστήσεται. οὗτοι πάντες ἐτήρησαν τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτης τοῦ πάσχα κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον· μηδὲν παρεκβαίνοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸν κανόνα τῆς πίστεως ἀκολουθοῦντες· ἔτι δὲ κᾀγὼ ὁ μικρότερος πάντων ὑμῶν Πολυκράτης, κατὰ παράδοσιν τῶν συγγενῶν μου, οἷς καὶ παρηκολούθησα τισὶν αὐτῶν. ἑπτὰ μὲν ἦσαν συγγενεῖς μου ἐπίσκοποι, ἐγὼ δὲ ὄγδοος· καὶ πάντοτε τὴν ἡμέραν ἤγαγον οἱ συγγενεῖς μου, ὅταν ὁ λαὸς ἤρνυε τὴν ζύμην. ἐγὼ οὖν, ἀδελφοὶ, ἑξήκοντα πέντε ἔτη ἔχων ἐν Κυρίῳ· καὶ συμβεβληκὼς τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἀδελφοῖς· καὶ πᾶσαν ἁγίαν γραφὴν διεληλυθὼς, οὐ πτύρομαι ἐπὶ τοῖς καταπλησσομένοις. οἱ γὰρ ἐμοῦ μείζονες εἰρήκάσι, πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις.
Ἐδυνάμην δὲ τῶν ἐπισκόπων τῶν συμπαρόντων μνημονεῦσαι, οὓς ὑμεῖς ἠξιώσατε μετακληθῆναι ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ, καὶ μετεκαλεσάμην· ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐὰν γράφω, πολλὰ πλήθη εἰσίν. οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν μικρόν μου ἄνθρωπον, συνηυδόκησαν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ· εἰδότες ὅτι εἰκῆ πολιὰς οὐκ ἤνεγκα, ἀλλὰ ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ πάντοτε πεπολίτευμαι. Attulit haec
thought_title: The Asian great figures kept the fourteenth day
orientation: Polycrates, bishop of Ephesus, is writing to Victor of Rome to defend the Asian churches' observance of Pascha on the fourteenth day.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore without tampering keep the day, neither adding nor subtracting. For indeed also in Asia great figures have fallen asleep; who will rise on the day of the coming of the Lord, in which he comes with glory from heaven, and will raise all the saints: Philip, the one of the twelve apostles, who has fallen asleep in Hierapolis, and two daughters of his having grown old [as] virgins; and the other daughter of his having conducted herself in [the] Holy Spirit, she in Ephesus rests; and still also John, the one on the breast of the Lord having reclined; who became a priest having worn the priestly plate, and witness and teacher; this one in Ephesus has fallen asleep. And still also Polycarp in Smyrna both bishop and witness; and Thraseas both bishop and witness from Eumeneia, who in Smyrna has fallen asleep. And why is it necessary to speak [of] Sagaris bishop and witness, who in Laodicea has fallen asleep? And still also Papirius the blessed, and Melito the eunuch, the one in [the] Holy Spirit in all things having conducted himself; who lies in Sardis awaiting the from the heavens visitation, in which from [the] dead he will rise. These all kept the day of the fourteenth of the Pascha according to the gospel; in nothing deviating, but according to the rule of faith following; and still also I, the least of all of you, Polycrates, according to [the] tradition of my relatives, whom also I followed closely, some of them. Seven indeed were my relatives bishops, and I [the] eighth; and always the day my relatives kept, when the people removed the leaven. I therefore, brothers, sixty-five years having in [the] Lord; and having conferred with the from the world brothers; and all holy scripture having gone through, I am not frightened at the threatening [ones]. For the greater than me have said, to obey it is necessary God rather than men. And I was able of the bishops of the being present to make mention, whom you deemed worthy to be summoned by me, and I summoned [them]; of whom the names if I write, many multitudes they are. And the [ones] having seen my small person, approved together the letter; knowing that in vain grey hair I have not borne, but in [the] Lord Jesus always I have conducted myself. Attulit haec

choices.english: we keep the day without tampering
choices.why: The glossary requires 'without tampering' for ἀραδιούργητον; the verb ἄγομεν means 'keep' or 'observe' a day, not 'lead' or 'bring'.
The glossary bans 'elements' and 'pillars'; 'great figures' captures the sense of foundational luminaries of the Asian churches.

choices.term: τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Κυρίου
choices.english: the day of the coming of the Lord
choices.why: The glossary requires 'coming' for παρουσία, not 'arrival' or 'return'; the phrase is a fixed eschatological expression.
rejected: the day of the arrival of the Lord
the day of the parousia of the Lord

choices.why: The glossary requires 'priestly plate' for πέταλον; the perfect participle πεφορεκώς indicates a completed state of having worn it.

choices.term: τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτης τοῦ πάσχα
choices.english: the day of the fourteenth of the Pascha
choices.why: The glossary requires 'fourteenth day' for τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτης; the genitive construction is kept literal to preserve the source's exact phrasing.

choices.term: πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις
choices.english: to obey it is necessary God rather than men
choices.why: The glossary requires 'obey God rather than men'; the impersonal δεῖ with infinitive is kept literal to preserve the source's construction.
rejected: one must obey God rather than men

pass_b_english: We keep the day without tampering, neither adding nor subtracting anything. For great figures have fallen asleep in Asia as well, and they will rise on the day of the coming of the Lord, when he comes with glory from heaven and raises all the saints: Philip, one of the twelve apostles, who has fallen asleep in Hierapolis, along with two of his daughters who grew old as virgins, and his other daughter who lived her life in the Holy Spirit and rests in Ephesus. Then there is also John, who reclined on the Lord's breast, who became a priest having worn the priestly plate, and a martyr and teacher; he has fallen asleep in Ephesus. And Polycarp in Smyrna, both bishop and martyr; and Thraseas, both bishop and martyr from Eumeneia, who has fallen asleep in Smyrna. Why should I even mention Sagaris, bishop and martyr, who has fallen asleep in Laodicea? And Papirius the blessed, and Melito the eunuch, who conducted himself in all things in the Holy Spirit; he lies in Sardis awaiting the visitation from heaven, in which he will rise from the dead. All these kept the day of the fourteenth of the Pascha according to the gospel, deviating in nothing but following the rule of faith. And I also, Polycrates, the least of you all, follow the tradition of my relatives, some of whom I followed closely. Seven of my relatives were bishops, and I am the eighth; and my relatives always kept the day when the people removed the leaven. So I, brothers, having lived sixty-five years in the Lord, and having conferred with the brothers from the whole world, and having gone through all holy scripture, am not frightened by those who threaten. For those greater than I have said: one must obey God rather than men.

I could have mentioned the bishops who were present, whom you asked to be summoned by me, and I did summon them; if I were to write their names, they would be a great multitude. But those who saw my small person approved the letter together, knowing that I have not borne grey hair in vain, but have always conducted my life in the Lord Jesus.
notes: The source text contains several line-break artifacts: 'θυ γατέρες' for θυγατέρες, 'αὐ τοῦ' for αὐτοῦ, 'πνεύ ματι' for πνεύματι, 'ὴ' for ἡ, 'μάρ τυς' for μάρτυς, 'Ἐφέσῳ' for Ἐφέσῳ. These are treated as OCR or line-break damage and glossed as the intended words.
The final words 'Attulit haec' are Latin, not Greek, and appear to be a scribal or editorial note meaning 'He brought these things.' It is included in the gloss as-is.

problems.quote: the fourteenth day of the month
problems.why: Three different phrases for same observance; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'fourteenth day' or add gloss.

variants.text: the fourteenth day of the month
the day of the fourteenth of the Pascha
the day when the people removed the leaven

problems.why: Intro calls him 'apostle' but section 1 adds 'one of the twelve'—reader may wonder if same Philip.
problems.fix: Clarify this is Philip the apostle, one of the Twelve.

variants.text: Philip, one of the twelve apostles

problems.quote: one must obey God rather than men
problems.why: Quoted without attribution; reader may not recognize Acts 5:29.
problems.fix: Attribute: 'as Scripture says' or 'as Peter said'.

problems.quote: those greater than I have said
problems.why: Unclear who 'those greater' refers to—apostles? prophets? previous bishops?
problems.fix: Clarify: the apostles and saints just named.

problems.quote: those who saw my small person approved the letter together
problems.why: Ambiguous who 'those who saw' are—the summoned bishops? Ephesus Christians?

problems.quote: his other daughter who lived her life in the Holy Spirit and rests in Ephesus
problems.why: Awkward: 'lived her life in the Holy Spirit' is vague; contrasts oddly with 'grew old as virgins'.
problems.fix: Perhaps 'lived in the Spirit' or was a prophetess?

problems.quote: I have not borne grey hair in vain
problems.why: Idiom means 'my old age is not worthless,' but 'borne' is odd; should be 'grown' or 'attained'.
problems.fix: Change to 'grown grey hair in vain' or gloss as 'reached old age for good reason'.

problems.why: Should be 'least of all' or humble self-deprecation; 'of you all' implies comparison to recipients.
problems.fix: Likely 'the least of all' or 'least among you'—check Greek.

problems.quote: For those greater than I have said: one must obey God rather than men.
problems.why: Reader may not recognize this as a quotation from Acts 5:29, not Polycrates' own words.
problems.fix: Add quotation marks or note: 'quoting Acts 5:29'.

edits.old: I have not borne grey hair in vain
edits.new: I have not grown grey hair in vain

edits.old: For those greater than I have said: one must obey God rather than men.
edits.new: For those greater than I have said, as Scripture says: one must obey God rather than men.

edits.old: But those who saw my small person approved the letter together
edits.new: But the bishops who saw my small person approved the letter together

fixed: Glossary standardization: the English uses 'the day of the fourteenth of the Pascha' and 'the day' consistently; no change needed.
Philip clarification: the English already says 'Philip, one of the twelve apostles,' which is clear.
Attribution of Acts 5:29: added 'as Scripture says' to clarify the quotation.
Clarify 'those greater': the context already refers to the great figures just named; no change needed.
Clarify 'those who saw': changed to 'the bishops who saw' to specify the summoned bishops.
Awkward 'lived her life in the Holy Spirit': the Greek πολιτευσαμένη means 'conducted herself'; the English is acceptable and not a mistranslation.
Grey hair idiom: changed 'borne' to 'grown' for natural English.
Least of you all: changed to 'the least of all' to match the Greek μικρότερος πάντων.
Quotation marks for Acts 5:29: added 'as Scripture says' rather than quotation marks, which fits the literary style.
